title: The Runaway Golem
hook: Heartlands. Old Nan Borrow's root cellar has walked off. That is not a figure of speech. Every morning for a week the brickwork cellar door has been found farther from the house, dragging root vegetables with it like a guilty child. Nan wants her pantry back, and the soot-covered dwarven scholar squatting in her herb patch wants you to catch the thing before it crosses the border into the Sootworks mines.
premise:
The scholar, Grudd Coalwatch, will not tell you in plain words what the cellar actually is. He mutters about apprentice mistakes and a runaway prototype, and he smells of coke-oven smoke and shame. His master left Sootworks forty years ago after some embarrassment nobody speaks of, and the cellar-thing is that embarrassment coming home to roost.

The Heartlands hedgerows are not designed to stop two tons of walking masonry. Hares scatter. A milkmaid swears loudly at you, thinking you are responsible. The trail is plain: a furrow of flattened wheat, a broken stile, a single smoke-stained stone dropped at a crossroads like a clue. If you follow it into the Sootworks mine shaft at the border, the golem will wedge itself in the tunnel and refuse to move, waiting for orders it was never given.

steps.objective: Find Nan Borrow's missing cellar before the milkmaids find you first
steps.flavor: A furrow of crushed barley leads southwest, broader than any plough.

steps.objective: Follow the trail of dropped turnips and broken stiles to whatever is pulling the thing home
steps.flavor: Coal-smoke in the air grows thicker with every mile.

steps.objective: Get the golem unstuck from the mine mouth and teach it what 'go home' means in a language it was built to hear
steps.requires: Grudd's repair manual, one tin whistle
steps.flavor: The cellar door shivers, waiting. Something in it remembers being told a task.

twist: The golem is not running away. It is going home. Grudd's master built it to carry tools from the house to the forge every dawn, and it has been doing so for forty years, confused that the forge has moved and the house has filled with turnips. When you whistle the shutdown sequence from the manual, it kneels in the mineshaft and weeps rust.
resolution: Grudd coaxes the golem to sit at the border mine, where it becomes a doorstop and a shortcut both. The tunnel it cleared on its rampage is now a navigable pass between Heartlands and Sootworks. Grudd gives you the repair manual in thanks, muttering that you will need it for the others.
unlocks_prose: The cellar-thing settles at the Heartlands-Sootworks border and will let you climb through its open hatch to cross between the two regions without taking the long road. You keep a grimy leather-bound book stamped with a master's sigil; it lets you issue simple commands to any golem you meet, which you will meet more of than you expect.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Nan Borrow
dialogue_beats.line: It took my onions, dearie. It took my ONIONS. Bring back what you can. Keep the beetroot, I don't much care for beetroot.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Grudd Coalwatch
dialogue_beats.line: Aye, it's his work. You can tell by the joinery. Master never could resist a proud seam. Mind the whistle — C above middle, not the D. D gets it digging.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the golem
dialogue_beats.line: (a long grinding sigh, like a millstone remembering being a hill)

title: The Tide Pool Collector
hook: Saltbrine Reach. Low tide. A barefoot woman with a belt full of jars is kneeling in a rock pool, hissing at a crab. She is Lenna Fathomkeep, and she collects the fish that only show themselves for twenty minutes a day. If you can stand the smell and the seaweed underfoot, she will teach you how to see them.
premise:
Saltbrine's proper fishermen go out deep, for lobster and kraken and what nets bring up. Lenna fishes the margins — the six inches between wet rock and dry rock, the puddle-left-behind, the crack no bucket fits into. The fish she catches are tiny, strange, and worth more than cod to the right cook. Nobody has catalogued them properly because nobody else can be bothered.

She wants a net. Not any net — a net of the exact wrong size for the open sea, woven with a loose middle so a sand-gudgeon can stay tangled but a seacup can pass through. She cannot weave it herself because her hands shake now. She also cannot bend down as long as she used to, and that is why she is hissing at the crab instead of catching it.

steps.objective: Let the crab go and hear Lenna out
steps.location: Saltbrine Reach, the shingle north of the harbour
steps.flavor: Gulls argue overhead. The tide is turning, which means the lesson has a deadline.

steps.objective: Find somebody who still remembers how to weave a shallow-net with a torn heart
steps.requires: a coil of light twine, two cork floats
steps.flavor: The old weaver's hands will tremble, but his mouth remembers every stitch.

steps.objective: Fish one of each thing Lenna names, without touching any of them with bare skin
steps.location: the tide pools at true low water
steps.flavor: The sandgudgeon bites. The seacup stings. The glasseel will make you forget your own name for an hour.

twist: Two of the species Lenna lists do not exist in any Saltbrine records. You will have to decide whether to tell her the tide pools are changing, or pretend you caught exactly what she described. She is watching your face when you come back.
resolution: Honesty wins her; she laughs, and admits she stopped updating her list thirty years ago because listing a thing is the beginning of the end of it. She hands you the net. The tide pool spots are yours to work whenever the water falls low enough, and the catch will be yours alone.
unlocks_prose: You walk away with a slack-hearted net, the only one of its kind in Saltbrine, that catches fish nobody sells at market. Cooks in three regions will pay you silly for a jar of glasseel. The tide pool shelves are open to you at every ebb — you just have to know when the water goes, and nobody will tell you twice.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Lenna Fathomkeep
dialogue_beats.line: Not a seine, you great lump. A seine will drown a seacup. I want a net with a hole in its soul.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Old Weaver Mollesh
dialogue_beats.line: Haven't woven a margin-net in... oh. Since my Berta died. She kept them on the line. They dry funny.

title: Lamplighter's Apprentice
hook: Moryskah border at dusk. The lamps along the old post road are going out one by one, and the lamplighter — a thin man named Voss, who walks with a beech pole and hums an old song — is losing ground to the dark. He needs an apprentice, not for wages, but because something is following him from lamp to lamp and he would rather not be followed alone.
premise:
The Moryskah lamps are older than the post road. They were set down when the swamp was first named, by a guild of lighters who made pacts with the things that live between lit and unlit. The lamps do not run on oil. They run on being tended by a known hand. When Voss is the only hand, the thing that follows remembers him too clearly.

There is a particular tinderbox, kept in a particular box, in a particular cupboard in Voss's cottage. His master gave it to him the night she stopped coming home. It lights blessed wood on the first strike, which matters when the swamp air will not take a flame. Voss will lend it to you tonight if you walk the lamps with him, and he will let you keep it if you walk the loop alone tomorrow without dropping one.

steps.objective: Shadow Voss on his route and learn why he hums that particular song at every third lamp
steps.flavor: The wick takes the flame like a mouth takes a wafer. The thing at the edge of the light holds its breath.

steps.objective: Gather the small wooden offerings each lamp expects — different at each post — before you go round again
steps.requires: a twist of wolfsbane, a coin minted before the war, a child's milk tooth left by parents who had no better grave
steps.flavor: Nobody asks why you want these things. Everybody knows.

steps.objective: Walk the route alone at moonset and light every lamp without looking directly at what is watching you from between them
steps.flavor: The third lamp is where the hum starts. If you forget it, the lamp will not forget you.

twist: The last lamp on the route is dark, and the metal is cold, and the offering in the pan is gone — taken before you got there. You must choose: skip it (Voss says one missed lamp is survivable, two is not), or relight it with what you carry on your own person (the bracelet, the brooch, the lock of hair from the person you miss most). Neither choice is wrong. Both are remembered.
resolution: You return to the cottage at dawn. Voss is alive, which he was not certain he would be, and he hands you the tinderbox in both hands. He tells you to come back on the shortest night of the year to walk the route with him, or for him. The lamps along the border are yours to travel now, each to each, without the road in between.
unlocks_prose: You carry a tinderbox shaped like a squat iron acorn, worn smooth by two lifetimes. It catches any wood you strike it over, blessed or cursed, and the Moryskah border lamps now recognize your hand. Touching a lit lamp lets you step to any other lamp on the route as if the road between them had been folded up and put in a drawer.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Voss
dialogue_beats.line: Hum at the third one. You don't have to know the words. It just has to hear the tune.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Voss
dialogue_beats.line: Master said: the lamps are our manners. What we light, we greet. What we let go dark, we owe.

title: The Apprentice Trapper
hook: Veilwood. The canopy above your head is so thick the sun only reaches the floor as coin-sized pools. Someone has been climbing up there, and they have been leaving traps that go off in daylight and catch birds instead of chinchompas. A furious elf called Sylven Brightknot is confiscating any trap she finds and she would like a word with you about the word 'permit'.
premise:
The Veilwood canopy is not legally a place. It is a negotiated understanding between the trees and the people allowed to climb them. Outsiders who set traps up there catch things they should not, and disturb things that had agreed not to be disturbed. Sylven is not angry because you broke a law. She is angry because you nearly broke a promise that predates your grandparents.

To set traps in the canopy you need a permit, which is not a paper. It is a length of spidersilk tied round the wrist, and the spider it came from has to remember you tying it. Sylven will take you to meet the spider. The spider is the size of a cart. You will be fine, probably, depending on what you have in your pockets.

steps.objective: Surrender every trap you have set and listen to Sylven tell you what you nearly killed
steps.flavor: She pulls a sparrow from a bent wire and strokes its head until it stops trembling.

steps.objective: Bring the old spider something it will accept from a stranger
steps.requires: a pelt from a creature you hunted and ate yourself, a comb carved from bone, a word you do not often say out loud
steps.flavor: The spider does not speak. It regards. There is a difference.

steps.objective: Set your first legal trap where Sylven points, and wait for whatever comes
steps.requires: spidersilk wristband, a box trap of the right shape
steps.flavor: A moonhawk lands on your wrist like a held breath.

twist: The spider accepts two of your three gifts but demands a fourth: the next thing you catch, whatever it is, belongs to her, and you must carry it home uneaten. If you try to cheat by catching something small, she knows, and the band tightens.
resolution: You bring her a chinchompa. She eats it in a way you will dream about for weeks. The spider nods once. Sylven pretends not to have seen. You are now among the few outsiders who may set traps above the moss line.
unlocks_prose: A thread of spidersilk sits tight around your wrist, and it has a memory. In the Veilwood canopy, traps you set now hold. Rare chinchompas, moonhawks with feathers like split mirrors, and the slow bright-eyed lemur nobody has named yet — they are yours to catch, within reason, and the permit does not come off except by the weaver's own legs.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Sylven Brightknot
dialogue_beats.line: You did not steal. Theft has a shape. What you did has no shape, which is worse.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Sylven Brightknot
dialogue_beats.line: She will like you or she will not. Do not smile at her. It confuses her.

title: The Stolen Runes
hook: Heartlands. The rune shop on Tannery Row was robbed last night, and the robber took nothing valuable — they took the three cheapest stacks on the counter and left the expensive ones untouched. The shopkeeper, Ruven Mourn, is more offended than frightened, and he has the right instincts: if you steal the cheap runes, you are planning something that needs a lot of them and cannot afford to be noticed buying them.
premise:
Ruven has been selling runes in the Heartlands for thirty-one years. He knows every regular by the way their coin lands on the counter. He also knows a bad spell when he hears it being prepared, and somebody is preparing one: the pattern of stolen stacks (earth, air, mind) is a beginner's binding. Somebody inexperienced is trying to tie down something they should not.

The thief dropped a pouch on the way out the back door. A rune pouch, stitched in the old style, with three inner chambers. It belonged to Ruven's own apprentice, long gone. He does not want to say the name. He wants you to find her before she casts whatever she is casting, and bring her home.

steps.objective: Examine the counter, the back door, and the pattern of missing stacks. Tell Ruven what you think was being planned
steps.flavor: The till is untouched. The shelf-dust tells you more than the ledger does.

steps.objective: Find the apprentice, using only what the dropped pouch tells you and what Ruven will not say
steps.location: Heartlands outskirts, a cottage nobody visits
steps.flavor: The apprentice's mother still lives. She will not like being visited.

steps.objective: Stop the binding without breaking it. Break a binding badly and whatever is inside comes out angry
steps.location: an abandoned chalk circle in the woods
steps.requires: a flask of river water, and patience
steps.flavor: The circle is half-drawn. You arrive exactly as she reaches for the final rune.

twist: The apprentice is not binding a demon. She is trying to bind her own grief, which is a creature of sorts, and it does not want to be bound. You must decide whether to let her finish — unorthodox, ill-advised, but hers to try — or convince her to walk back with you and tell Ruven why she left in the first place.
resolution: Either choice sends her home. Ruven waits in the shop doorway, arms crossed, and when she reaches him his crossed arms come apart. He hands you a pouch that isn't the dropped one — it is his own, much finer, and he has not stitched one in twenty years. He also tears up the old ledger and writes your name on the first page of a new one, with a discount beside it.
unlocks_prose: You carry Ruven's Rune Pouch — three inner chambers in supple leather, stitched with his sigil, and it holds three different runes without their ever mixing. The rune shop knows your face now, and when you push coins across the counter a quiet tenth of them is pushed back. Nobody else in the Heartlands gets that price.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Ruven Mourn
dialogue_beats.line: They took earth. Air. Mind. The rest they left. That's not a thief, that's a student, and a sad one.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the apprentice
dialogue_beats.line: If I do not bind it I will carry it forever. If I bind it wrong it carries me. There is no good option. Only mine.

title: The Fencepost Problem
hook: Heartlands ranch country. Every morning, three fenceposts on Arun Bellfield's eastern pasture are lying on the ground, and no animal has knocked them down. Arun has stayed up at night with a lantern and a strong drink and seen nothing. He is convinced, with the calm of an exhausted man, that his fence hates him personally. He would like a second opinion.
premise:
The Bellfield ranch has stood where it is for four generations, and the eastern fence has always been the problem fence. Arun's grandmother built it without asking the field what it thought. The field has opinions. It has been politely raising its fenceposts out of the ground, one at a time, for longer than anyone alive can remember, and Arun is the first to notice in several decades because he is the first to need the pasture for real cattle rather than sheep.

The fix is not more fence. The fix is a small bell hung on a particular post, rung once at dawn, and then left alone. Arun's grandmother left instructions in a drawer nobody has opened since she died. The bell is also in the drawer. It is very small and it looks like a joke.

steps.objective: Walk the fence with Arun at dawn and watch it happen. Then ask him if anyone in his family left any notes
steps.flavor: The post in the middle lifts itself out of the earth like a tooth giving up.

steps.objective: Find the grandmother's instructions in the drawer nobody will open, and the bell in the jar behind them
steps.location: Bellfield ranch house, the back room
steps.flavor: The drawer sticks. A hairpin in the keyhole will not do what a polite word does.

steps.objective: Hang the bell on the post the grandmother marked. Ring it once. Do not ring it twice
steps.location: the middle of the eastern fence
steps.flavor: The field sighs, which is a sound you will pretend you did not hear.

twist: The bell is not on the post the grandmother described. Her directions are correct, but the field moved while you were gone. You will have to walk the pasture until you find where the post wants to be, and set the bell there instead. If you get it wrong the bell rusts through within a week.
resolution: Arun watches you get it right, which is to say he watches his pasture stop fighting him, and for the first time in two years he looks unfrightened. He gives you a keyring with a bell on it that is a miniature of the big one, and he tells you the gate of the ranch will open to anyone wearing that bell, no matter where they are in the Heartlands.
unlocks_prose: The Heartlands ranch is yours to travel to, bell in hand, as if the road had folded itself up to bring you there. You also carry a Rancher's Bell on a cord; ring it somewhere quiet, and a pet cow comes plodding over, which is cosmetic and very much welcome, and which sets a farming timer you will rely on.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Arun Bellfield
dialogue_beats.line: She left a drawer I was told not to open. I have respected this for three decades. Today I will disrespect it.

dialogue_beats.speaker: grandmother's note
dialogue_beats.line: Ring once. The field is not deaf, it is tired. Tired things do not like to be shouted at.

title: The Bog Witch's Errand
hook: Moryskah. A woman in a coat made of crow feathers and hessian is standing in a swamp up to her knees, and she is waiting for you specifically, though you have never met. She is the Bog Witch's hedge-daughter Merenna, and she has a shopping list from her mother, and her mother does not like to come into town.
premise:
The Bog Witch does not do her own shopping because the last time she did, three stalls closed and one horse refused to ever be ridden again. Merenna is her errand-girl, and Merenna is tired, and Merenna wants a proper adventurer to run the list today because her feet are swollen and the swamp tea has done nothing.

The list is not a normal list. It is read out loud, not handed over, and it changes depending on what the witch is brewing. You will be told a set of things. Most of them are everyday. One or two are strange. All of them have to come back clean. If you run the list well, the witch will teach her hedge-daughter to teach you, which is how herblore gets passed down in this part of the world.

steps.objective: Memorize Merenna's list without writing it down — she will not repeat it, and ink attracts flies in the bog
steps.flavor: A rusted hinge. Three salt-cured eels. A bell no-one has rung in a century. The thing your mother threw away when you were nine.

steps.objective: Gather the items. Do not explain what they are for if asked, because you do not know
steps.location: Moryskah village, the abandoned chapel, and somewhere only you know about
steps.requires: patience; a polite refusal if the miller gets curious
steps.flavor: The bell in the belfry is heavier than it has any right to be.

steps.objective: Return to Merenna before the sun drops below the line of cattails, or the witch starts the brew without you
steps.flavor: Merenna counts them with a finger. Her finger does not touch them.

twist: One of the listed items cannot be purchased: the thing your mother threw away when you were nine. The quest journal will not help. Merenna will not help. You must decide, yourself, what that was, find something that stands for it, and bring it. The witch will know if you lied.
resolution: The brew bubbles green and then silver and then a colour you do not know the word for, and the Bog Witch — finally visible from a shack that was not there when you arrived — grunts once and nods. Merenna smiles for the first time that day. The witch hands you a small pot of salve that smells of turned earth and mint, and a short list of plants that will grow for you, not for other people, in a herb patch that is now yours to tend.
unlocks_prose: You walk away from the swamp with a bruise-coloured salve that keeps undead at arm's length long enough to matter, and the recipe for it, which uses no ingredient you cannot acquire. A corner of the Moryskah bog now grows swamp herbs for you, the sort that hedge-witches swap at harvest time and never sell. The Bog Witch does not wave. She never waves.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Merenna
dialogue_beats.line: I am not going to tell you the list twice. If you forget a thing, pick something that rhymes with it. She hates that, but she respects it.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the Bog Witch
dialogue_beats.line: The ninth thing is the only real one on the list. The other eight are a courtesy.

title: Target Practice
hook: Heartlands militia range. Captain-at-Arms Odette Brume is shouting at a line of recruits who cannot hit a hay bale at twenty paces, and she needs someone to shoot decent enough to shame them into competence. If you can put three arrows on a moving mark without flinching when she barks, she will give you a badge that means something.
premise:
The militia range has a daily practice hour nobody but regulars attend, because the regulars are famously mean to walk-ins. Odette runs it. She was an archer in a war she does not name and she trains the way she was trained, which is harder than necessary and better than civil. The badge she hands out is stamped on pewter and it looks like a child's toy. It is not.

To earn it you have to prove you can learn, not prove you can shoot. Odette will make you do something deliberately awkward — shoot left-handed, shoot in wet gloves, shoot at a target she has numbered backwards — and she will watch whether you complain. If you complain, the badge goes to someone else, and you will not get another chance this season.

steps.objective: Turn up at the morning hour and take whatever odd instruction Odette hands you
steps.requires: a bow you can actually draw
steps.flavor: Rain spatters the hay. The recruits smirk. They are going to lose that smirk.

steps.objective: Shoot the awkward shot she designs for you without comment
steps.flavor: Your gloves are full of water. The string feels wrong. Good.

steps.objective: Do it again tomorrow without being asked
steps.flavor: Odette nods once. The recruits do not smirk today.

twist: On the second morning Odette will be absent. A sergeant will lie and say the drill is cancelled. If you leave, you fail. If you stay and practise on your own, Odette will appear from behind the targets — she was watching — and hand you the badge in silence.
resolution: The badge pins to the inside of your coat, close to the heart, which is where the militia say it belongs. Odette tells you the range is open to you every morning now, and that if you bring a friend who shoots worse than you, the friend will be laughed at, but tolerated.
unlocks_prose: You carry a Militia Archer's Badge, dented and warm, and at the Heartlands range your arrows fly truer than they ought to. A daily bonus of steady ranged training is yours whenever you can spare the hour — low attention, high effect — and the sergeant has learned your name, which matters more than it sounds.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Odette Brume
dialogue_beats.line: If you speak when the arrow is in the air, you have already missed. Speak afterwards if you must. Preferably not.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Odette Brume
dialogue_beats.line: The badge is pewter. The shot is not.

title: The Boneyard Compass
hook: Boneyard Wastes, the last oasis before the deep dunes. Cartographer-at-Large Imrat Keshvu is unrolling a map so blank it is nearly paper, and he would like you to help him fill it. The sandstorms have been worse this year. His last two assistants walked east and came back west, confused and thirsty. He has a compass that might or might not be a compass.
premise:
Boneyard sandstorms disorient on purpose. They are the old empire's last defence, and the empire has been dead long enough that the defence has forgotten what it is defending. The storms turn travellers in circles and make north taste like south. You can get around this with water, luck, or a very particular kind of compass.

Imrat's compass was given to him by a hermit who would not explain it. It is a needle in a bowl of sand, and the needle points at whatever the compass decides is important today. Imrat thinks he has worked out how to ask it for north. He thinks. He would like to be wrong in your company rather than alone.

steps.objective: Listen to Imrat's theory and decide if it is worth walking into a sandstorm to test
steps.requires: a canteen full, a second canteen full
steps.flavor: The map crackles in the dry air. The compass is already pointing at something.

steps.objective: Test the compass in the storm. Do not drink the second canteen until the first is gone
steps.flavor: The needle jerks when you think about home. Which home is not specified.

steps.objective: Return on a bearing the compass chooses for you, and see where you come out
steps.flavor: You step out of a dune-wall into Imrat's oasis, but from the wrong side, and he is laughing.

twist: The compass does not point north. It points at whatever you have most recently promised yourself you would do. If you have nothing to promise, it spins. Imrat will not tell you this until you have survived one storm without it.
resolution: Imrat takes the compass back in ceremony, and then gives it to you, because he has already drawn every map he wanted to draw and you are younger. He marks your face with a thumb of ochre. The storms will still come, but they will no longer take you anywhere you did not intend to go.
unlocks_prose: A bowl-compass rides at your belt, and in the Boneyard dunes its needle obeys your intention, not the magnetic poles. Sandstorms no longer turn you around; you walk through them with your water intact. The deep dunes are open to you, and the things out there that kept their distance before now have no reason to.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Imrat Keshvu
dialogue_beats.line: The hermit said: it points at what you will not forgive yourself for not doing. I told him that is a long phrase for a bit of needle. He said: and?

dialogue_beats.speaker: Imrat Keshvu
dialogue_beats.line: Drink the first canteen. Do not drink the second. That is the only rule in the dunes.

title: The Slayer's First Mark
hook: Heartlands. At the back of the militia barracks, behind a door with a bronze tusk nailed to it, a shaven-headed youth named Kael is trying to assign slayer tasks to a man twice his age who won't stop calling him 'lad'. Kael is one task away from quitting. You look competent. He will give you a first mark right now if you take it without arguing.
premise:
Slayer is not hunting. Hunting is what you do when you choose the quarry. Slayer is what you do when someone else chooses. The first mark is a test of obedience — not to Kael, who is twenty and afraid, but to the idea that killing a thing you would not have thought to kill teaches you something about both the thing and yourself.

The mark is drawn in chalk on your palm. It names a creature, a place, and a count. The chalk will not rub off until you finish. If you give up, it stays, and every slayer master in Aelgard will look at it and refuse you the next mark until you come back and close this one.

steps.objective: Accept the mark without asking what it is. Look at it after the door shuts
steps.flavor: Kael presses the chalk into your hand. His hand is shaking, which he would rather you did not mention.

steps.objective: Find the creature the mark names in a part of the world you probably have not thought about today
steps.requires: a weapon you trust, a willingness to walk
steps.flavor: The mark glows faintly when you are close. It tugs when you are far.

steps.objective: Finish the count. Bring back something small from the last kill, not a trophy, just proof
steps.flavor: Kael weighs it in his hand. He nods, chews his lip, says nothing that would sound final.

twist: The mark will include one creature you would not have killed for money — a thing more pitiful than dangerous. Kael is watching to see whether you finish the mark the way it is written or whether you pretend. If you pretend he will know, and the next mark will be harder.
resolution: Kael wipes the chalk off your palm with his own thumb and adds a tally to a ledger nobody else will ever read. He says: come back tomorrow. He means it. The door with the bronze tusk will open for you now without the youth having to nod first.
unlocks_prose: Kael will assign you novice slayer tasks from now on — kills that give Slayer training, structured combat work, and the slow respect of an apprentice master learning his own trade on you. You also carry a crumb of slayer-chalk in a twist of paper, kept for a day when you need to mark your own hand.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Slayer Apprentice Kael
dialogue_beats.line: I am not supposed to hesitate. I am hesitating. If you make fun of me, I will give you the goblins, and you will be there a week.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Slayer Apprentice Kael
dialogue_beats.line: Proof is a tooth or a claw or a button. Do not bring me a head. I hate heads.

title: The Counterfeit Ring
hook: Saltbrine Reach, the customs office. Inspector Calla Bright has a tray of forty-three rings on her desk, and thirty-eight of them are fake. The other five are almost certainly fake too; she has not yet been able to prove it. The ring she cannot prove is the one she wants you to follow, because whoever made it is better than any forger she has ever arrested.
premise:
Saltbrine's smuggling trade runs on counterfeit jewellery. A good fake wedding ring will carry a diamond that is not a diamond through three ports. A better fake will carry the provenance papers of a dead noblewoman. The very best fakes are not copies of real rings — they are copies of rings that never existed, backed by forged histories so complete that the fake has a better paper trail than the truth.

Calla has been chasing the ringmaker for two years. She cannot go herself because her face is known. She will lend you her loupe, which belonged to her mother, and ask you to attend a masked auction at the Cove where the ringmaker is rumoured to be selling a new line. She will not tell you what you are looking for. She wants to see if you can tell.

steps.objective: Look at the tray of rings with Calla's loupe. Point out which one you think is the one she cares about
steps.flavor: Forty-three rings. Calla does not blink when you pick one up.

steps.objective: Get an invitation to the Smuggler's Cove auction without using the word 'customs'
steps.requires: a small favour owed to a bosun, a coat that hides your calluses
steps.flavor: The password changes nightly. Tonight's is a gull's name nobody would say on shore.

steps.objective: Attend the auction. Spot the ring the ringmaker brought. Do not buy it
steps.requires: the loupe, a mask, hands that do not sweat
steps.flavor: The ringmaker is not on the stage. The ringmaker is in the audience, and you recognize their ring on their own finger.

steps.objective: Follow the ringmaker after the auction without being seen, and learn where the forge is
steps.flavor: They walk without looking back, which is how people who know they are safe walk.

steps.objective: Bring Calla the forge's address. She will decide what to do with it
steps.requires: a clear memory of the route
steps.flavor: She writes down three things. Two she burns. One she keeps.

twist: The ringmaker is the previous inspector, Calla's predecessor, who retired under no shadow and was farewelled with a party Calla attended. Calla will not tell you this until you come back with the address. She will then ask you what you think should happen. The answer is yours.
resolution: Whatever you decide, Calla thanks you by entrusting you with the loupe permanently, and by opening the Cove's back gate. You can now trade there, which is useful for selling things you would rather not be asked about.
unlocks_prose: You carry the Inspector's Loupe on a cord, and false things announce themselves to it — coins, gems, seals, your luck at a dockside card game. The Smuggler's Cove's back gate opens to you now; the market there pays better than any legal house and asks fewer questions. Calla still returns your nod on the street.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Inspector Calla Bright
dialogue_beats.line: Forty-three rings. Thirty-eight I can prove, five I cannot. Tell me which of the five you dislike and we will see if we dislike the same one.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the ringmaker
dialogue_beats.line: You have my mother's loupe. I know you have it. I am not angry. I am only surprised she gave it up.

title: Sand and Secrets
hook: Boneyard Wastes, the edge of the excavation camp. Archaeologist Veris Sankhara has dug a hole the size of a barn into a dune, and from the bottom of the hole she is shouting in three languages at something she thinks is a door. She has run out of diggers willing to work past sundown. She thinks the door has opinions about that.
premise:
The Wastes bury things. That is what they do. When an archaeologist finds a thing, the Wastes resist — sandstorms cover the dig overnight, workers wake up with small injuries they do not remember, the finds migrate in their crates. Veris does not take this personally. She has been doing this for twenty years. She simply works faster than the desert can fill in, and she is close to something real.

The door at the bottom of her pit is older than the Aelgardi calendar. It has writing in an alphabet her books do not name. It also has a keyhole, and the keyhole is the shape of a thing she has seen in three of her diggers' dreams in the last month. She wants to open it. She would also like to be fairly sure, before she opens it, whether it is a door in or a door out.

steps.objective: Climb into Veris's pit and look at the door with your own eyes. Form an opinion before she tells you hers
steps.requires: a head for sand, boots with laces you trust
steps.flavor: The writing on the door is not carved. It is grown, as if the stone remembered being told.

steps.objective: Find the dreamers. Ask what shape the keyhole is, without showing them the keyhole
steps.requires: patience, a bottle of sharp wine for the one who will not speak without it
steps.flavor: Three diggers. Three dreams. Three descriptions that agree, which is the wrong number of times to coincide.

steps.objective: Have the key shaped — do not ask the local smith. Go to Sootworks and ask a specific one
steps.requires: a sketch of the keyhole, a piece of desert bone
steps.flavor: The smith raises an eyebrow. Then she raises the other one, which means she is impressed.

steps.objective: Return. Open the door. Do not step through first
steps.flavor: The door opens the way a yawn opens. Air comes out that has not been breathed in a long time.

steps.objective: Look at what is on the other side. Report to Veris honestly
steps.requires: a lamp, a short rope tied around your waist in case
steps.flavor: There is a floor. There is a ceiling. There is a room, of sorts, and it has been waiting.

twist: The door is a door out, not in. Something small, patient, and not hostile walks past you into the Wastes while you stand there. Veris watches it go and says nothing for a full minute. Then she says: I suppose that is fair.
resolution: Veris grants you access to the dig. The pit becomes a staircase, the staircase becomes a foothold, and the Wastes roll back from you a little. She teaches you how to quarry the sandstone that did not exist before the door opened — softer, more workable, with veins that show.
unlocks_prose: The Boneyard Wastes are open to you now as a place you may work in rather than a place that works on you. You know the sandstone quarry, the one the desert grudgingly permits, and you can AFK the strike of the pick for bars of warm, grainy stone. What walked out of the door is somebody else's quest.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Archaeologist Veris Sankhara
dialogue_beats.line: A door does not mean an entrance. Doors have two sides. Somebody put this one here to keep a thing from coming out, or a thing from going in. We will find out which, once it matters less.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Archaeologist Veris Sankhara
dialogue_beats.line: I will not tell the university about the dreamers. Universities do not like dreams.

title: The Green Thumb
hook: Heartlands farmstead. Farmer Aldwin's beet crop is dying a colour beets should not die. The black crust is spreading from row to row. Aldwin has tried lime, ash, and a priest. Nothing. The old herb-woman who visits his mother says the cure is in Veilwood, and the elves will not sell it, and Aldwin is too old to crawl through a forest that does not like visitors.
premise:
Veilwood does not sell soil. Soil is not, to an elf, a thing that can be owned or traded. It is a relationship. You do not cure a sick field by buying a bag of Veilwood earth, because the bag would sulk in your cart and refuse to wake up when you tipped it out. You cure a sick field by bringing the field to the Veilwood, or by bringing a Veilwood druid to the field, or — and this is the real answer — by learning the Rootsong, which is a way of asking a field to remember what health felt like.

Elder Marwen knows that the Rootsong exists. He does not know it himself. The druid Archdruid Elara knows it and will teach you, reluctantly, if you bring her proof that the field wants to be healed. Proof, to a druid, is five Moonroot bulbs pulled up by someone the forest did not attack on the way in.

steps.objective: Walk Aldwin's field with him at dawn. Take a bark sample from the great ash at the edge of it — the ash is dying too, just slower
steps.flavor: The bark peels like old paper. Beneath, the wood is streaked black.

steps.objective: Reach the Veilwood druid circle without being turned around by the forest. This means walking softly and talking less
steps.requires: your samples, a mouth you can keep shut for an hour
steps.flavor: The moss reads the soles of your boots. You are being evaluated every step.

steps.objective: Pull five Moonroot bulbs from the forest floor without bruising the skin of any
steps.location: Veilwood forest floor, south of the circle
steps.flavor: A bulb turns in your fingers and looks at you. It will not do that twice, if you handle it right.

steps.objective: Brew the soil restoration potion under Elara's watch, then chop a living branch from the Heart-Oak with her blessing
steps.flavor: The water is sacred because Elara said so. That is enough.

steps.objective: Perform the grafting ritual at moonlight on Aldwin's field. Do not let the first pass of blighted insects spoil it
steps.location: Heartlands farm, under a near-full moon
steps.flavor: The insects come in three waves. The field is listening. You do not stop singing between waves.

twist: Elara will not teach you the full Rootsong. She teaches you the first verse. The second verse must be learned from the Heart-Oak directly, which means asking a tree a question and waiting until it answers, which takes longer than you have. The field recovers without the second verse, but you will notice the lack later, in another farmer's field, when you go back.
resolution: Aldwin's beets come back green, slowly. The Great Ash puts out leaves it had given up on. Elara pins a seed pouch to your belt — a dibber that places seeds at the correct depth without your having to think about it — and tells you the Veilwood herb patches are open to a hand that has sung for them.
unlocks_prose: Veilwood is open to you as a place to grow things in, and the herb patches there accept your seeds as properly offered. You carry a druid's planting dibber that does not miss. You also know the soil restoration potion recipe, which keeps a field from getting sick for a full hour of watching — enough time to run a crop through without disease.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Farmer Aldwin
dialogue_beats.line: Priest came. Said a blessing. Beets got worse. I do not hold him responsible, but I noticed.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Archdruid Elara
dialogue_beats.line: You do not buy a cure. You borrow the memory of health and give it back in spring. If you keep the memory for yourself you will not notice, at first, that your own colour is worse.

title: Foundations of the Fallen
hook: Heartlands, the eastern moor. The Chapel of the Last Light has been a pile of stone for a hundred years, and everyone in the village of Wellcote has been pretending it is not there. A mason called Perla Goodknee wants to rebuild it. She has asked every guild in the Heartlands, and every guild has said the same thing: the old chapel was built by Sootworks hands, and nobody up here knows the joints.
premise:
The Chapel of the Last Light fell because the villagers took the altar slab to make a millstone and the roof followed a year later. It was built in the old Sootworks joint-style, where each stone is cut so that its neighbour supports it directly and mortar is barely needed. Nobody in the Heartlands remembers the cuts. The dwarves still use them, but they do not teach them to outsiders. Foreman Grukk in the Steam District will consider it, if you prove you can smith the bracket-iron his apprentices use to hold a joint-cut in place overnight.

Rebuilding the chapel is the job. Discovering what the villagers are pretending not to know is the other job. The altar slab was not taken for a millstone. There is a crypt under the chapel floor, and the slab was moved to cover the stair.

steps.objective: Walk the ruin with Perla and decide with her what can be re-used. Mine limestone from the chapel quarry only if you can name the bed it came from
steps.location: Heartlands, Chapel of the Last Light
steps.requires: a pick, an eye for stone
steps.flavor: Perla kneels by a fallen lintel and runs a fingernail along its underside. She whistles, low.

steps.objective: Travel to the Sootworks Steam District. Convince Foreman Grukk you are not wasting his time by smithing the test brackets without complaining
steps.flavor: The forge is loud enough that Grukk's criticism is almost inaudible. Almost.

steps.objective: Learn the joint technique. Lay the foundation in the old way. Raise four wall segments correctly — Perla will check each one
steps.location: Heartlands, Chapel of the Last Light
steps.flavor: Perla presses her palm flat against each wall and listens with her ear to the stone. Two she nods at. One she tells you to take down.

steps.objective: Build a pulley yourself and raise the roof beam without help. Light the chapel lantern when it is up
steps.location: Heartlands, Chapel of the Last Light
steps.flavor: The lantern catches. Something under the floor moves, very slightly.

steps.objective: Investigate what the lit lantern revealed beneath the altar. Report honestly to the Heartlands Archives
steps.flavor: The crypt is dry. That is the first wrong thing about it.

twist: The Sootworks joint-style the dwarves teach you is an older form than the chapel actually used. When you lay the foundation, one joint does not fit, and you will realize — either on your own or when Grukk arrives uninvited — that the chapel was built by a dwarf who had been banished for inventing a new cut. Grukk wants to know what the old heretic built, and what is under it.
resolution: The chapel stands again. Perla weeps politely and pretends she is not weeping. Grukk examines the crypt and takes notes in a book he does not let you see. You have rebuilt a shrine and uncovered a secret, and both are now yours to revisit.
unlocks_prose: The Sootworks is open to you as a region, not just a border mine. You have the joint-cut technique in your hands, and construction XP flows better when you use it — a small bonus per wall, per beam, per rebuilt doorway. The hidden crypt beneath the chapel is yours to enter when you are ready, and it has its own quiet appointments.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Perla Goodknee
dialogue_beats.line: A chapel is just a box you agreed to pray inside. I don't care what you believe. I care that the box stands.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Foreman Grukk
dialogue_beats.line: Bracket-iron. Five. No complaining. If I hear one word about your back, you get the bellows for a week.

title: The Bog Witch's Bargain
hook: Moryskah. Father Dorin has finally walked out to the bog witch's shack because the wolves at the village edge have stopped being wolves. He wanted to pray over it. The witch Grael has told him praying is a fine thing but a boring thing, and that she will help him if, and only if, he brings her an adventurer who will run three errands she does not trust a priest with.
premise:
Grael does not do bargains lightly. A bargain is a debt she can call in, and a bargain with a priest is a debt with interest. With an adventurer she can trade by the hour. The werewolves in the Moryskah woods are not cursed — they are remembering a shape they used to wear, and something is reminding them. Grael knows who. She wants that person dealt with in a way Dorin would not approve of, and she is happy to teach you herblore properly as payment.

To prove you are worth teaching she wants three things done: a wolfbane incense blended from plants she will point at but not name, a name pulled out of a witness who will not give it to a priest, and a visit to a grave that has to be walked to, not ridden to. If you do all three in the right order, she will tutor you in proper swamp herblore, and the Moryskah as a region will stop eyeing you sideways.

steps.objective: Meet Grael at the shack she did not have last week. Hear the bargain. Do not sign anything
steps.requires: a strong stomach, nothing written down
steps.flavor: Father Dorin is waiting outside, looking at his shoes. Grael has three chickens on her roof.

steps.objective: Blend wolfbane incense from plants you gather in the Moryskah deep swamp. Grael will watch from a distance and say nothing until you finish
steps.flavor: Three of the plants bite. One is a mushroom that watches you back.

steps.objective: Visit the witness. Do not threaten them. Get the name out using only words and a cup of tea
steps.location: a hut behind the Moryskah windmill
steps.requires: patience, the right sort of tea
steps.flavor: The witness is a girl of nine with a grandmother's mouth. She drinks her tea in one long sip.

steps.objective: Walk the long graveyard path to the grave Grael has circled on a scrap of map. Do not let anyone carry you any part of the way
steps.flavor: The graves along the path belong to every family in the village. Half the names are crossed out in paint that has not weathered.

steps.objective: Return to Grael with the incense burning and the name on your tongue. Hand them both over
steps.requires: the lit incense, the spoken name
steps.flavor: Grael does not touch the incense. She bows to it, a fraction.

twist: The name is the name of a man Father Dorin baptized, and he was not told because Grael knew he would refuse to let her act. Dorin will find out. You will have to choose whether to stand between them when the argument starts, or to step back and let the swamp arbitrate.
resolution: Grael burns the incense for three nights. The wolves at the village edge go back to being wolves. Father Dorin and Grael are not friends, but they are cordial on feast days now. Grael opens her pantry to you and starts teaching properly, which turns out to be harder than the bargain.
unlocks_prose: Moryskah is open to you as a region — all of it, the wet parts and the dry, and the bits with signs — and Grael the Bog Witch is your herblore tutor for the advanced swamp potions nobody else will teach you. You know the wolfbane incense recipe; burn it and werewolves find somewhere else to be for a good ten minutes. The incense stains your sleeves and it stains your thinking, which Grael says is the point.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Grael the Bog Witch
dialogue_beats.line: A priest is a rope with a knot tied at both ends. He cannot do the untidy bits. That is what we are for, you and me. Only you have a shorter memory, which helps.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Father Dorin
dialogue_beats.line: I asked you to come here to pray. I see you have done something else instead. I will not ask what.

title: Pirate King
hook: Saltbrine harbour, under a sky the colour of a bruise. The harbour is closed because three pirate frigates sit at its mouth and nobody has yet worked out how to politely ask them to leave. Harbourmaster Cole drinks his breakfast from a tankard and tells you the only way into the pirate flagship is to be invited, and the only way to be invited is to lose a fight to their bosun.
premise:
The Pirate King is not a king. He is an administrative invention — the captain the other captains defer to because he has the best cook, the best charter, and the only copy of the trade wind almanac that is not ten years out of date. If he moves his fleet, Saltbrine opens. If he refuses, Saltbrine starves. Cole has been trying to negotiate for a week. The pirates are bored. They would like a duel.

You will lose the duel on purpose because the winner gets chained in the bilge and the loser gets the captain's table. Then you will eat, drink, steal the almanac, and decide whether to betray the Pirate King, befriend him, or replace him. The charter-ship network of Aelgard's coasts runs on his signature. However you leave that ship, the signature has to come with you.

steps.objective: Find the bosun on the dock and lose a fight to him without looking like you meant to lose
steps.requires: a willingness to bleed, an understanding of pride
steps.flavor: The bosun is enormous, cheerful, and smells of butter. He apologises while he hits you.

steps.objective: Accept the invitation to the captain's table. Eat everything offered. Drink what you can
steps.flavor: The cook is as good as advertised. The almanac is in a bookcase behind the captain's chair.

steps.objective: Find a reason to be left alone in the great cabin for four minutes
steps.flavor: A steward returns after three minutes. You have the almanac or you do not.

steps.objective: Decide how you are leaving the ship. Each way pays differently
steps.flavor: The Pirate King has not asked you a direct question. He is waiting to see if you will ask one of him.

steps.objective: Return to Cole at the harbour. Tell him what arrangement you reached, and what signature came with you
steps.flavor: Cole listens without interrupting, which for him is extraordinary.

twist: The Pirate King is Cole's sister. She was the harbourmaster before he was, and she resigned to go to sea because somebody in the city wanted her quietly dead. Cole will not tell you. The King will. You have to decide whether Cole is told, when Cole is told, and in whose voice.
resolution: The fleet moves. Saltbrine breathes. Cole reads the almanac at his own desk and does not thank you, which is his way. The Pirate King sends a gift: a hook-handle in brass, and a charter-ship pass stitched into the sleeve of a coat that fits you.
unlocks_prose: The Saltbrine Reach is open to you and the charter-ship network is yours — you can pay passage between coastal ports as a regular traveller, which collapses the map. You carry the Captain's Hook, a cosmetic blade and a real benefit: your fishing goes faster when you are working from a boat. People on the docks give you the nod, the one that means you know the King.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Harbourmaster Cole
dialogue_beats.line: Lose the fight. Do not let him see you lose on purpose. He would rather lose on accident to an honest hand than win against a liar.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the Pirate King
dialogue_beats.line: I do not take the harbour. I visit. When I visit, the harbour chooses to close. That is a different thing and it matters.

title: Slayer's Gauntlet
hook: Moryskah Slayer Tower, top floor. Slayer Master Varrek does not turn around when you come in. He is watching a spider through a window and taking notes. He will acknowledge you when you have killed a monster of each combat style and brought back the proof. He will not tell you which monsters. He will, however, offer tea.
premise:
Varrek is old, and old slayer masters do not take on students. They already have their name engraved somewhere. He is considering taking you on because Kael wrote him a letter, which is not something Kael does often. Varrek wants to see whether the apprentice's hunch holds.

The gauntlet is three kills, one per style. The monsters are your choice. If you choose badly — killing something that is obviously easy for you — Varrek will assign you harder work next time. If you choose honestly — a monster you are not confident about — Varrek will make your next work easier, because he will trust you to pick your own difficulty.

steps.objective: Choose a melee quarry that will test you. Bring back the proof Kael told you about
steps.requires: a melee weapon, the right attitude
steps.flavor: Spiders in the Moryskah cellar are the easy choice. The giant up the hill is the better one.

steps.objective: Choose a ranged quarry. Do not pick something that stands still
steps.flavor: A dark wizard moves. A training dummy does not.

steps.objective: Choose a magic quarry. Not a thing you would ordinarily throw spells at. Something that you think will make you better if you succeed
steps.flavor: The hill giant is not usually killed with magic. That is rather the point.

steps.objective: Return to Varrek in the order you killed. Set the proofs on his desk. Say nothing until he asks
steps.flavor: He counts without looking up. He already knew the count.

twist: Varrek will have watched one of your kills from a distance without your knowing. If you cheated, he knows. He will not accuse you. He will simply assign your next task as if you had failed, and you will notice.
resolution: Varrek pours tea. He tells you the Tower's upper levels are yours to climb when you choose, and the intermediate tasks are available from his desk from now on. He gives you a gem that shows the current mark in its facets, wherever you are.
unlocks_prose: You can receive slayer tasks from Varrek directly, which are harder and pay better than Kael's, and the Moryskah Slayer Tower is open to you above the second floor, where the creatures actually earn you a keep. An enchanted gem rides in your pocket; held to the light, it shows your current mark's shape, so you know what you are hunting without having to go back to ask.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Slayer Master Varrek
dialogue_beats.line: Bring me proof. I do not care what you took it from. I care whether you were scared while you took it.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Slayer Master Varrek
dialogue_beats.line: Tea. Sit. You talk more quickly when your hands are busy.

title: Sootworks Rising
hook: Sootworks Level 5, the deep vent gallery. Something is moving inside the blast furnace, which is not unusual — but it has been moving for a week, and nothing has come out. Forgemaster Brun has posted a bounty he does not expect to be paid out on. He needs someone who can walk up to a door that might be the inside of a stomach and open it anyway.
premise:
The Sootworks has rebuilt the Blast Furnace three times in living memory. Each time it has rebuilt itself slightly differently, because the smiths who rebuild it are always angry about something. The current furnace is sullen, efficient, and old. For the last week it has been smelting without ore, and the slag coming off the tap is the colour of lamp oil.

Inside the furnace, the old smelting-golem is still at its station. Nobody has spoken to it in forty years. It is doing its job and nobody has told it to stop. Shutting it down requires walking in through a vent that a person your size can fit through if you remember which way is up, and saying a shutdown phrase that only one retired dwarf remembers, and the retired dwarf lives in a Boneyard oasis he refuses to leave.

steps.objective: Meet Brun at the furnace. Take his measure. Decide whether to be paid now or later, because he will not pay twice
steps.flavor: Brun's beard is singed to a uniform length, which is how you can tell he is careful.

steps.objective: Travel to the Boneyard oasis where the retired dwarf is drinking his retirement. Bring him something from home
steps.location: Boneyard Wastes, the old dwarf's oasis
steps.requires: a bottle of coal-beer from the Sootworks, patience
steps.flavor: He does not turn around when you come up. He waits for you to say your name.

steps.objective: Learn the shutdown phrase. Write it down, then burn what you wrote down
steps.flavor: The phrase is three words, in a language the dwarf will not translate.

steps.objective: Return to the Sootworks. Climb the vent. Find the golem. Say the phrase without stammering
steps.requires: the phrase, a lamp that does not need air
steps.flavor: The golem is beautiful. You will have to be brave to speak.

steps.objective: Shut the golem down gently. Record its name in Brun's ledger. Do not tell Brun what the golem said last
steps.flavor: Something it said last you will remember for years.

twist: The shutdown phrase does not shut the golem down. It wakes the golem up, properly, for the first time in a lifetime. The golem asks you — politely — whether it may continue working. The choice is yours: let it stop and be idle, or let it keep working and be told what to do next. Both paths give the same unlock. The difference is whether you sleep well for the week afterwards.
resolution: Brun accepts your report. The Blast Furnace runs correctly again, faster than it did, and smiths start queuing for time on it. He gives you a right of use that survives his death, which he is not quiet about.
unlocks_prose: The Blast Furnace is yours to smith at; your coal doubles up, your bars come faster, your XP is better per hour than at any basic forge. You know the deep-stone alloy, which needs less coal than it has any right to, and the Blast Furnace as a training method is open — high attention, high XP, high profit, the proper Sootworks offer.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Forgemaster Brun
dialogue_beats.line: There is a thing inside. It has a name. It is not my name, and it is not your name, and if you say it wrong you will be inside too.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the old dwarf
dialogue_beats.line: Say the words like a son says goodnight to a father. Not afraid. Not loud. Say them once.

title: Into the Wilds
hook: Heartlands, the north gate. Ranger Tomas wears a coat that has been patched in three colours and does not match his hair. He is handing out warnings to anyone who looks like they might walk north, and he is not stopping anyone. He will, however, talk to you about the Wilds, and about the one supply cache that nobody has come back for in two months.
premise:
The Wilds are lawless because the laws do not survive being written down there. Ranger Tomas teaches the survival the way it is taught in the Wilds themselves — short, cold, and with a willingness to walk away from anything that is not moving in the direction you need. The supply cache was left by a forward party that did not come back. The party is dead. The cache is not.

You will walk in, pick up the cache, and walk out. Everything else about the Wilds — the player-against-player rule, the predator density, the absolute indifference of the land to your name — you will either learn on the way or you will not come back. Tomas is not your friend and does not pretend to be. He will, however, teach you the one thing that keeps rangers alive: the trick of not looking at what is looking at you.

steps.objective: Hear Tomas out. Do not ask questions that Tomas will not answer
steps.flavor: He does not sit. He paces. He never finishes a sentence in one breath.

steps.objective: Walk to the abandoned ruins. Do not run. Running in the Wilds means something to the things that watch
steps.requires: walking boots, a short sword, resolve
steps.flavor: The sky here is a flat grey. It does not change colour when the sun moves.

steps.objective: Recover the supply cache from wherever the party hid it when they realised they were not going to come back
steps.flavor: The cache is behind a fallen beam, under a folded cloak, still folded, as if someone meant to come back for both.

steps.objective: Escape back to the border without being seen more than once. The agility shortcut exists if you find it
steps.requires: a map you mostly remember, hands ready
steps.flavor: You will be seen once. Only once is survivable.

twist: The cache contains a sealed envelope addressed to Tomas by name, in a hand he recognises. He will not open it in front of you. He will, however, give you the survival-kit he had been saving for the previous party.
resolution: Tomas does not thank you. He nods. You have walked in and walked out, and you have learned how to stand next to the Wilds without leaning in. The border gate is your door now; he will let you through without the warning.
unlocks_prose: The Wilderness Agility Course is open to you, and it is the best agility training-per-hour in Aelgard — if you can stand being in a PvP zone while you use it. You carry a Ranger's Survival Kit: a one-click teleport straight to the Wilds border, usable once, which has saved better rangers than you.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Ranger Tomas
dialogue_beats.line: Do not look at the things that are watching you. If you see them, they are now real to you. If they are real to you, they can reach you. Eyes down, walk past.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Ranger Tomas
dialogue_beats.line: The envelope is my problem. Your problem is whether you come back tomorrow.

title: The Inkweald Door
hook: Inkweald boundary. The border is not a line, it is a mood: the trees on the inside are wrong in a way you cannot point at, and the trees on the outside are watching them. Lucid Keeper Yara sits in a tent pitched where the mood changes, and she has been sleeping too little, and she wants to know if you have had any unusual dreams lately.
premise:
The Inkweald is a dreaming, and Yara is its hinge. She is the Keeper, which means she sits where the dream meets the world and keeps the door open — not for travellers, but for the dream itself, which must breathe. The door is weakening because somebody inside the Inkweald is holding their breath. If the door closes wrong, the Inkweald collapses in on itself and everything inside it becomes a memory nobody owns.

To stabilize the door you must enter it and find the person who is holding their breath, and convince them to let it out. Yara cannot go herself because she is the hinge. She will teach you the first verses of dream magic — NPC-contact, dream-teleport, lucid-ward — if you can close the door without slamming it.

steps.objective: Sleep where Yara tells you to sleep. Describe the dream you have, in detail, before you are fully awake
steps.flavor: Yara writes your dream on a slate. She does not look at you while you tell it.

steps.objective: Step through the door on the second night. Do not use your name inside. Dreams are fond of names
steps.requires: a small token to exchange for the use of a name
steps.flavor: The air on the other side feels like reading.

steps.objective: Find the person holding their breath. They will not be visible until you stand close enough to hear them
steps.location: Inkweald, wherever the breath-holding is loudest
steps.flavor: A painter. A printer. A mapmaker. A child who has not blinked in some time. You decide which, and you will be mostly right.

steps.objective: Convince them to breathe. Do not use logic. Dreams do not respect logic
steps.requires: a story you have not told anyone
steps.flavor: They breathe out, eventually. You breathe in. It is not fair.

steps.objective: Return through the door. Tell Yara only what she asks. Do not volunteer what you saw
steps.flavor: Yara nods once. She writes a second slate and sets it on top of the first.

twist: The person holding their breath is you, in a sense — a dream-version of you who was left behind on a previous visit to the Inkweald you cannot remember having made. You must convince yourself to breathe. You will know how to do this only after you have tried the wrong ways.
resolution: The door stabilizes. Yara teaches you the first verses of dream magic, which are strange and helpful and do not always work in the way you would expect. The Inkweald opens to you as a region, and the border is no longer a mood — it is a door, with your name on the inside.
unlocks_prose: The Inkweald is open to you, every shifting acre of it, and the Dream Magic spellbook is yours — a utility spellbook, full of the sort of spells that save you steps rather than killing anything quickly. NPC-contact to speak across the map. Dream-teleport between places you have actually dreamt. Lucid-ward to keep things out while you sleep. None of it glamorous, all of it indispensable.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Lucid Keeper Yara
dialogue_beats.line: The Inkweald is not dangerous. It is unwell. The difference matters. You are not going to fight it, you are going to sit with it.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the breath-holder
dialogue_beats.line: If I breathe out I am not sure what shape I will be next. I would rather be this shape. You understand.

title: Desert Treasure
hook: Boneyard Wastes, the Pyramid's outer courtyard. An archaeologist in black silks and a sun-bleached scarf is pacing around a scale model of the pyramid she built herself, and she is counting diamonds on her fingers. Four diamonds. Four regions. Four guardians. She wants the Ancient Magicks, and she cannot get them alone, and she has been waiting for someone who can cast a novice spell without flinching to finish what she started.
premise:
The Ancient Magicks were sealed out of Aelgardi practice by the Pyramid's first priesthood, who judged that the old spells killed too freely. The seal is four diamonds, set in four shrines, in four regions; break all four and the seal parts and the spellbook becomes readable. The diamonds are not guarded in the ordinary sense. They are bound: to ice, to shadow, to blood, to smoke. Each binding has a guardian, and each guardian is not a monster — they are judges.

Azzanadra is the name of the magician whose book this is. He is not in the book. He is, according to the archaeologist, watching. The Ancient Magicks include ice barrage, blood barrage, smoke barrage — the sort of spells that change how a fight ends. The seal was put in place for a reason. Breaking it is work.

steps.objective: Meet the archaeologist. Listen to her four-diamonds theory. Agree or disagree honestly
steps.flavor: Her scale model has moved since yesterday. She swears she has not touched it.

steps.objective: Find the Ice Diamond in the Glasswake Passage, north of the Glass Desert. Survive cold that is not temperature
steps.requires: firemaking for warmth, a willingness to be judged
steps.flavor: The cold asks you a question before you reach the diamond. The question is about a winter you do not often remember.

steps.objective: Find the Shadow Diamond in the Inkweald dream labyrinth. Do not trust your reflection
steps.requires: a dream anchor, an honest memory
steps.flavor: The labyrinth is a version of the pyramid laid on its side. The labyrinth knows.

steps.objective: Find the Blood Diamond in Castle Malachar. Defeat the blood guardian without taking the blood it offers you
steps.flavor: The guardian extends a goblet. Decline politely.

steps.objective: Find the Smoke Diamond in the Sootworks deep furnace. Survive heat that is not temperature
steps.requires: mining to dig the chamber out, nerves
steps.flavor: The smoke asks you what you burn for. You will not like your first answer.

steps.objective: Combine the four at the ancient altar in the pyramid. Read the spellbook while the seal breaks
steps.flavor: The altar recognises the shape you have made. It does not like the shape, and it permits you anyway.

steps.objective: Defeat the final guardian who rises as the seal parts. Do not use the Ancient Magicks against it, unless you want your first spellbook memory to be a fight
steps.flavor: It is old, and tired, and offering you the book with one hand while it fights with the other.

twist: The fourth guardian is not a guardian. It is Azzanadra, or what remains of him, and he wants you to take the book because he is finally done carrying it. You must decide whether to accept the book at face value, or to ask what he would like done with his name once it leaves his mouth.
resolution: The Ancient Magicks are yours. The pyramid does not close behind you — it opens further. The deeper chambers are accessible now, and they are quieter than you expect, because the book was the loud thing.
unlocks_prose: You carry the Ancient Magicks spellbook — ice barrage, blood barrage, smoke barrage, and the terrifying lesser spells that are quieter than their names suggest. The Boneyard Pyramid is open to its interior; the lower floors contain training no other place offers, and secrets you will uncover at your own pace.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the archaeologist
dialogue_beats.line: Four diamonds, four shrines, four regions. The seal is clever. The seal was not meant to be permanent. If it was permanent it would not be a seal, it would be a wall.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Azzanadra
dialogue_beats.line: Take the book. I have been its librarian long enough. Do not read it aloud where a child might hear.

title: Lunar Diplomacy
hook: Inkweald. Lucid Keeper Yara, who you have met before, is leaning over a bowl of moon-lit water and tracing circles that do not close. She says a word you do not know, and then she says it again, and then she asks if you would like to visit a place that is not usually a place. The place is called the Lunar Plane. The visit requires sleep.
premise:
The Lunar spellbook is not foreign magic. It is domestic magic, of the quietest sort. Heal a friend, cure a poison, call a distant NPC, condense humid air into a tool you forgot to bring. The Lunar elders live on a plane reached only through deep sleep, and they are not enthusiastic about visitors. They are, however, contract-minded. If you come to them on a business footing and complete the trials they have written down (literally written, which is rare, because they usually leave things implied), they will teach the spellbook.

The trials are not combative. They are demonstrations. Mine a lunar rock, which you will find is as much about listening as swinging. Light a sacred flame, which will go out if you take yourself too seriously. Craft a staff from dreamwood and crystal, which requires the staff's permission. You can brute-force none of it. Yara will teach you how to brew the dream-potion that gets you there, but after that the Lunar Isle is yours to prove yourself to.

steps.objective: Brew the dream potion under Yara's eye. Do not substitute ingredients
steps.flavor: The potion smells of a distant room. When it is ready, Yara nods once.

steps.objective: Sleep. Reach the Lunar Plane. Introduce yourself politely to whoever is there
steps.flavor: The Plane is a long white beach and three low buildings. The tide is the wrong direction.

steps.objective: Mine a lunar rock. Do not strike it. Ask it for a piece, and wait
steps.flavor: The rock gives up a chip when it is ready. You will not know it is ready until it is.

steps.objective: Light the sacred flame. Do not use a tinderbox first. Use breath
steps.flavor: The flame catches on the third try. The first two tries are allowed only because everyone's first tries are.

steps.objective: Craft the lunar staff. Ask before shaping. Thank after
steps.flavor: The staff vibrates when you are doing it right. It goes still when you are doing it wrong.

steps.objective: Convince the Lunar elders to teach you. Speak from below, not across
steps.requires: a reason that is not about power
steps.flavor: They already know. They want to hear you say it.

steps.objective: Wake up. Bring the spellbook back. Tell Yara what you saw, and what you said
steps.flavor: Yara's circles close for the first time while you tell her.

twist: The Lunar elders will offer you two spells as a parting gift — one that is listed in the spellbook, one that is not. The unlisted spell has a cost the book does not name. You will have to decide, in the moment, whether to accept both. The correct answer differs by player.
resolution: The spellbook is yours. The Plane remains accessible through sleep, not easily, but reliably. Yara returns to her bowl of moon-lit water and goes on tracing circles that close now. You have a new kind of quiet to draw on.
unlocks_prose: The Lunar spellbook is yours — cure, vengeance, heal group, NPC contact, humidify, and the others, the quiet spells, the ones that save a friend's life at fifteen paces. The Lunar Plane is accessible through sleep and ritual, and the Plane has a runecrafting altar nobody in Aelgard has published directions to.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Lucid Keeper Yara
dialogue_beats.line: The Lunar people will not fight you. That is not a reassurance. It means that if they refuse you, there is no fight to win. Walk softly.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Lunar elder
dialogue_beats.line: We teach because you asked from below. Those who ask from above do not visit twice.

title: Echoes of the Deep
hook: Sootworks, deep mine gallery. A pick has been ringing against the back wall of Level 7 for three days, and nobody is holding the pick. The vibrations are synced with tremors felt in Moryskah, and sandstorm patterns in the Boneyard, and a low hum in the Glass Desert that only dogs notice. Something underground connects all four regions, and it is waking up.
premise:
Aelgard's four inland regions sit on a single ancient machine. The old empire built it to hold the crust still. The machine has run correctly for ten thousand years because nobody has thought about it. Somebody is thinking about it now, and that is a problem. Until the source of the thinking is found and stopped, the tremors will get worse, and eventually a region will fall into the gap.

The tunnel network connecting the regions is not on any map. It has to be walked to be known. You will start in the Sootworks deep mine, follow the tunnel south to the Boneyard, follow it east to Moryskah under the swamp, and follow it further east to the Glass Desert where the machine's core is. At the core you will find the thing doing the thinking. It will not be a villain. It will be a device that has been left on.

steps.objective: Descend to Sootworks Level 7 and find the tunnel behind the ringing pick
steps.requires: a pick, a lamp, a reason
steps.flavor: The pick stops ringing when you are ten paces away. It starts again when you turn back.

steps.objective: Follow the tunnel south to the sealed chamber under the Boneyard pyramid. Open the seal with magic, not force
steps.requires: magic, the confidence to be refused once
steps.flavor: The seal opens on the second try. The first try is a courtesy to the old architects.

steps.objective: Continue east under Moryskah. The flooded section will try to drown you. Prayer keeps the water out, not the undead
steps.flavor: Undead watch you from beyond the lamplight and do not come closer. They remember the machine too.

steps.objective: Reach the core. Look at the thing that is thinking. Do not speak first
steps.flavor: It is a wheel the size of a cathedral, and it is turning very slowly, and on the wheel are names you know.

steps.objective: Shut down the wheel's spurious thinking without shutting down the machine. This means breaking the correct conduits, not all of them
steps.flavor: One bad strike and the machine stops. Stopping the machine is a different quest.

steps.objective: Report to Crystal Sage Orin with honest numbers. Do not inflate. He will know
steps.flavor: Orin was not surprised by the report. He was surprised you survived it.

twist: The spurious thinking is not accidental. Somebody put it there, long ago, as a fail-safe in case the machine was ever required to think for itself. You can switch off the thinking, but you will have to decide whether to leave the fail-safe installed for the next person, or to remove it and leave the machine as the architects intended.
resolution: Orin's palm bears a new scar when he shakes your hand — the machine pays its respects. The Glass Desert is open to you, and the underground tunnel is now a proper travel route. You know what Aelgard sits on, which is a weight no one asked you to carry.
unlocks_prose: The Glass Desert is open to you and the underground tunnel network — Sootworks to Boneyard to Moryskah to Glass Desert — is a travel route you may use when you please. Crystal mining nodes are open to you at the Glass Desert end: the highest-tier ore in the game, in a region most players never see.

dialogue_beats.speaker: Crystal Sage Orin
dialogue_beats.line: You have walked under the four regions. You now know something the gods did not quite tell me. I would like to know it too. Later, when you are less tired.

dialogue_beats.speaker: the wheel
dialogue_beats.line: (names turning past, including yours, three places off the top)

title: Dragon Slayer of Aelgard
hook: Sootworks, the Iron Vein foundry. A family of metal dragons has moved into the deep mines, which is not unprecedented, and they are not eating the miners, which is. They are, however, moving the ore. Forgemaster Brun wants the dragon-head off in a polite and structured way, because killing the mother-dragon wrong will make the whole family worse.
premise:
Metal dragons are hatched, not born; their mothers are often as surprised as anyone. The Iron Vein family has an adamant matriarch who is old enough to remember when the Sootworks was a hole. She is not attacking miners. She is relocating them to a chamber that she wants to keep, and she expects them to understand why. Brun has read enough dragon-lore to know that a polite slaying is the best any of them will get, and he would like it done before the matriarch has time to lay again.
